Sean — thanks for the call earlier. Procurement asked me to put three items in writing so we can move the order form through our legal routing: 1) whether Acme will have exclusive ownership of AI-generated output (our product copies / decisioning model outputs) and any downstream rights; 2) what level of rights Redwood requires to retain or use our customer data / logs for model training or quality improvements; and 3) the scope of any feedback license (do you require a perpetual license to use our feedback for product improvements?).

I've attached a short SOW and our internal checklist (Acme_SOW_and_requirements.pdf). Procurement needs a clear redline or language we can present to our counsel — is it possible to get a single redlined Order Form that shows the carveouts (output attribution, non-commercial training opt-out) and an accompanying plain-language summary?

Target timeline: we aim to sign by next week if possible — procurement routing opens Thu 7/1.

Elena — appreciate the clear list. I've pulled legal and product together and attached a redlined order form (Redline_OrderForm_Acme_20260630.docx) plus a short FAQ in the doc that summarizes our proposed compromise. High level suggestion:

- Output ownership: Acme receives exclusive rights to customer-facing outputs and may use outputs in its products/services. Redwood retains the right to use aggregated, de-identified telemetry for platform analytics only.
- Training / data use: Redwood will not train or fine-tune models on Acme customer data or logs without explicit opt-in and a fee-based add-on. We propose a clause: "Customer Data shall not be used to train or improve models used to serve other customers absent Customer's prior written consent."
- Feedback license: Redwood requests a limited, non-exclusive, revocable license to use user feedback (e.g., labels, annotations) for product improvements and bug fixes, with a restriction that any model improvements incorporating identifiable Customer Data require a separate agreement.

If those bullets look OK I asked Laura to propose clean legal language and Ben to start procurement handoff (PO and SSO access). Can you confirm whether Acme needs the "exclusive" term to be absolute, or if a narrower "exclusive for customer productization" is acceptable? Absolute exclusivity triggers a few follow-on clauses we have to escalate.

Proposed next steps:
1) Laura to send suggested phrasing
2) Elena to share whether counsel will accept or wants negotiated durations/attributions
3) Ben to open procurement ticket and confirm billing entity

I attached the redline. If you can scan with your counsel quickly we can aim for signature by 7/2.

On Tue, Jun 30, 2026 at 11:42 AM Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Elena — appreciate the clear list. I've pulled legal and product together and attached a redlined order form...

Elena / Sean — I reviewed Sean's redline and proposed edits below (see attached Legal_Markup_MSA_Acme.pdf for full inline comments). Summary of my standing positions:

1) Output ownership: we can commit to granting Customer (Acme) exclusive rights to internal use and customer-facing productization of Outputs for the licensed Product(s). We will not assign title to Redwood models or underlying weights. Please note: "exclusive" should be qualified to the extent it relates to Outputs produced from Customer prompts for the licensed service. Absolute exclusivity across all contexts (e.g., future model variants with unrelated data) is not something we can accept without additional commercial terms.

2) Training/Feedback: the proposed clause "no training without opt-in" is acceptable. I propose a 12-month notice period for any change in data-processing practices and an audit right limited to security/compliance vendors. For the feedback license, we will accept a limited, non-exclusive license for product improvements, provided any use for model training on identifiable Customer Content requires a separate written license and (if requested) commercial consideration.

3) Attribution / Derivatives: Acme asked about downstream attribution and derivative claims. We should add a carveout that Redwood will not claim ownership of customer-created prompts or unique business logic embedded in Outputs. However, Redwood must retain the right to make non-identifying improvements to the service.

Ben — if Elena signs off on these points, please open the procurement ticket and attach the draft PO terms per our standard EO-billing flow.

Laura Bennett
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Legal_Markup_MSA_Acme.pdf (legal comments; 4 pages)
